![A Genos group chat with a thread open beside it](/lp/guide/en/chat.webp)

A problem comes up in chat. People discuss it, agree on a fix and name who will do it. Two weeks later someone asks why you did it that way.

## Why it is hard

The talk is in the chat tool, the task is in the tracker and the reasoning is in a document, if anyone wrote it. Nothing joins them. You search all three, find half the story, and ask the one person who remembers.

## How Genos helps

Chat, tasks and notes are in one workspace, and you can tie one piece of work together.

```flow
Talk in a thread
Make a task from it
Write it up in the task's note
Ask Genos later
```

In a thread, choose **New task linked to this thread**. The "we should do this" conversation becomes tracked work with an owner and a date, and the task keeps the way back to the discussion. On the task, its note holds the plan and the decision, next to its comments and history.

## What you get

- **The why stays with the what.** Open the task and the discussion and the write-up are right there.
- **Fewer repeat explanations.** Someone joining later can read instead of calling a meeting.
- **Nothing agreed and then forgotten.** The agreement is a task on a board, not a line in a scrolled-past chat.
- **Questions that work.** Genos AI can answer from chat, tasks and notes together, and links what it used so you can check. It reads only what you can open.

## A small example of the habit

The next time a thread ends with "OK, let's do that", spend a minute:

1. Make the task from the thread.
2. Give it an owner and a due date.
3. Write three lines in its note: what was decided, why, and what was ruled out.

A minute now saves a search later, mostly for people who were not there.

## How to start

Open a thread in any group or project chat and create the task from it. A thread can have one task. Members of the project can read and edit the task's note, so keep the plan there.

When you come back to it, use **Ask Genos about this task** in the task's menu to catch up quickly. Asking uses your plan's AI allowance.
